selected.name: Route choice named and mathematically motivated in context
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the answer makes its strategic choice of method explicit and mathematically motivated, judged against the question title. Look for: the route being named ('compare with the integral', 'generating functions', 'induction on the number of blocks'), a stated reason why this route works or is preferable here (avoids a hypothesis, gives the constant as well as the rate, handles the boundary case, is cheaper than the routine attack), and a stated boundary on where it applies. 10 = the answer says what it is doing and why that is the right lever for this problem, and the reason is a real mathematical reason -- e.g. three plainly typed lines reading 'induction on n breaks because the constant degrades; instead bound the sum by the integral, which is monotone and gives the sharp constant.' 0 = a computation is executed with no indication of why this route, no boundary of validity, and nothing a routine first attack would not already give. Do NOT reward length, LaTeX, headings, bullet lists, or bare signpost words: a lone 'Alternatively,' or 'Another approach:' with no mathematical reason behind it scores 0 here. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is correct, and do not consider whether any other post exists.
selected.rationale: The parent conflates a real craft property -- knowing which lever this problem wants and saying why -- with the surface habit of writing as though slotting into an ongoing thread. This component keeps only the reasoning: the judge must find a mathematical justification for the route, not a discourse marker. Two-way dissociation against D02 and D03: (a) high here, low there -- a five-line answer that opens cold with no restatement and no notation block (D02 = 0) and claims to be the complete solution with no scope hedging (D03 = 0) can still say exactly why the substitution u = tan(x/2) is forced by the pole at pi and score 10; (b) low here, high there -- an answer that opens 'Just adding a short remark, only for the case n = 2' (D03 near 10) and then spends its first paragraph restating the problem and fixing notation (D02 near 10) but simply grinds through algebra with no account of why that algebra scores 0 here.

selected.name: Extent of from-scratch setup in the opening lines
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer's opening (roughly its first three sentences or first display, whichever comes later) is spent re-establishing the problem before any new mathematics is done. Count the presence and bulk of: restating what is to be proved or computed, echoing or paraphrasing the question's own wording, fixing notation ('Let n be ...', 'Write f for ...', 'Throughout, p denotes ...'), listing hypotheses or standing assumptions, and framing sentences such as 'We want to show that ...' or 'The problem asks for ...'. 10 = the answer opens with a full restatement of the problem plus a notation or assumptions block before any step is taken. 5 = one orienting clause, then straight into the work. 0 = it begins mid-move with no orientation whatsoever ('Take logs.', 'Integrate by parts.', 'Set x = 1.'). Estimate the extent only; do NOT decide whether the orientation is helpful, well written, necessary, or redundant, and do NOT reward or penalise the mathematics that follows.
selected.rationale: This is one carrier of the unseen circumstance: text written into an empty thread tends to build the whole frame from the raw question, while text written later tends to drop straight into a move. It is a pure counting question about the first few sentences, deliberately different from D03, which ignores the opening entirely and asks about how much of a solution the post claims to deliver. Two-way dissociation against D01: (a) high here, low on D01 -- a long, carefully staged opening ('Let S = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k^2. We wish to evaluate S. Set a_k = 1/k^2.') followed by unmotivated grinding scores 10 here and 0 on D01; (b) low here, high on D01 -- 'Take logs; the product telescopes, which is why no estimate is needed here' scores 0 here and high on D01. Also dissociable from D03 in both directions: a from-scratch opening can be followed by 'this only settles the convergence half' (D02 high, D03 high on fragment posture), and a cold mid-move opening can still run to a boxed final answer (D02 = 0, D03 = 0).

selected.name: Scope posture: fragment or supplement versus whole solution
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer positions itself as LESS than the full solution. Base this on: explicit scope limiters ('just the key step', 'only the case k = 2', 'a short remark on why the hypothesis is needed', 'a hint', 'a shorter route to the same conclusion', 'this handles only convergence'); whether it stops deliberately before the final quantity or claim rather than reaching it; whether a sub-lemma, a special case, a refinement of a constant, or a sanity check is offered as the deliverable; and whether it is framed as an addition, aside, footnote, or correction rather than as the argument. 10 = the answer is openly a fragment, supplement, alternative route, special case, refinement, or remark and says so. 5 = mixed -- most of a solution with one part explicitly deferred or left to the reader. 0 = it presents itself as the complete self-contained solution, running from the problem statement to the final answer with no scope hedging. Estimate posture only; do NOT decide whether the narrower or broader scope is appropriate, and do NOT consider or speculate about any other post -- score only the framing visible in this text.
selected.rationale: This is the second, genuinely different carrier: not how the answer opens but how much of the job it claims. It is orthogonal by construction to D02 (opening orientation) -- posture is usually set by hedges and by where the text stops, which can occur anywhere in the post. Two-way dissociation against D01: (a) high here, low on D01 -- 'A small addendum: just the k = 2 case,' followed by two unexplained lines of algebra, scores near 10 here and 0 on D01; (b) low here, high on D01 -- a self-contained answer that never hedges its scope but explains that the whole point is to avoid the divergent term scores 0 here and 10 on D01. Dissociation from D02 in both directions is given in D02's rationale.

selected.name: Notation carries the argument, judged independently of typesetting
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the mathematical notation is chosen and managed so that a reader can actually follow the argument. Look for: every symbol introduced before it is used; index ranges, quantifiers and domains stated rather than left implicit; one letter with one meaning throughout (no silent reuse or collision); each equality or inequality in a chain traceable to a named reason or an obvious rewrite; the object being manipulated never ambiguous (function versus its value, sequence versus its limit, matrix versus entry). Judge the notation AS NOTATION, not as typesetting. An answer written entirely in plaintext ASCII -- 'sum_{k=1}^n 1/k^2', 'x^(1/2)', 'a*b', '3.68 x 10^-6' -- in which every symbol is introduced and used consistently and every sum has a stated range MUST be able to score 10. An answer dense with display environments, aligned blocks, cases, pmatrix, blackboard-bold, tags and macros whose letters collide, whose sums and products have unstated ranges, and whose displays are unlabelled chains with no stated reasons scores 0. Do NOT reward display environments, macros, equation tags, bold step labels, lists, or any markup at all; do NOT penalise plaintext or ASCII operators. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is correct.
selected.rationale: The parent fuses a genuine expository skill -- disciplined symbol management, so notation does argumentative work -- with the mechanical habit of typing in the site's markup. This component states the craft in terms that a plaintext post can satisfy fully and a heavily typeset one can fail entirely, and it forbids the judge from crediting any markup feature. Two-way dissociation against D05: (a) high here, low there -- a five-line ASCII answer defining 'let S_n = sum_{k=1}^n a_k, a_k > 0' and then reasoning cleanly scores 10 here and near 0 on D05; (b) low here, high there -- a post stuffed with align-star blocks, macros and tags whose x means three different things and whose sums have no index range scores near 10 on D05 and 0 here.

selected.name: Extent of LaTeX machinery versus ASCII mathematical orthography
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of site markup machinery present in the post, as a count or estimate. Raise the score with: number of inline maths spans and display equations; use of aligned, align-star, cases, matrix, pmatrix, array, and similar environments; equation tags and numbered back-references to them; macro definitions declared at the top of the post; blackboard-bold, script, boldface vector and other symbol conventions; and structural markup such as bold step labels, numbered or bulleted lists, headers, blockquotes and horizontal rules. Lower the score for mathematics typed as plaintext or programming-style ASCII -- '5^10 = 9,765,625', '3.68 x 10^-6', 'f(x) = a*x^{1/2} + bx', products written with asterisks, 'sqrt(2)', 'sum_{k=1}^n' -- and for formulas run into prose untypeset. 0 = no markup at all, everything in running plaintext. 5 = plain inline maths with a few displays. 10 = dense, multi-environment typesetting including macros, tags or structural furniture. Count the extent ONLY; do NOT decide whether the typesetting is pretty, professional, appropriate, or whether the mathematics is right.
selected.rationale: This is the mechanical carrier: keystroke habit with the site's editor, countable from the page without reading the argument. Two-way dissociation against D04 is stated in D04's rationale: a clean ASCII answer is 10/0 (D04/D05) and a macro-heavy answer with colliding letters and unstated index ranges is 0/10. Because the parent already correlates strongly with an existing lint feature, isolating the count here is what allows D04 to test whether any craft signal survives once the count is removed.

selected.name: Every load-bearing step supplied, once, nothing restated
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how completely the answer supplies the steps a competent reader could NOT reconstruct, and only those, judged against what the claim in the question title requires. Ask: is the crux -- the nonobvious substitution, the inequality that does the work, the convergence or interchange check, the case split, the base case that actually bites -- justified rather than asserted? Is each justification given exactly once? Is routine manipulation compressed rather than expanded? 10 = a four-line answer in which the single hard step is precisely the one explained and everything else is compressed to a phrase. 0 = the crux is waved through ('clearly', 'it follows easily', 'a standard argument shows') while elementary algebra is written out at length, or the same point is restated in three different ways. Do NOT reward word count, number of paragraphs, number of displays, section headers, or worked-out arithmetic: a long, elaborate post MUST be able to score 0 and a very short one 10. Judge only sufficiency per nonobvious step, not whether the result is correct, useful, or well presented.
selected.rationale: The parent measures bulk. The craft hidden inside bulk is not amount of text but justification where justification is scarce: closing the gap a reader cannot close alone, and not padding the gaps they can. Written as a ratio-like property, it is length-free by construction. Two-way dissociation against D07: (a) high here, low there -- three lines reading 'The interchange is the only issue; dominate by g = sup_n |f_n|, which is integrable by X, then pass to the limit' scores 10 here and near 0 on D07; (b) low here, high there -- a thousand-word post that expands every arithmetic simplification, repeats its plan twice, and then asserts the key inequality without argument scores near 10 on D07 and 0 here.

selected.name: Extent of sheer text volume, elaboration and repeated exposition
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of visible text and elaboration. Estimate: total length (roughly, 0 = under about 40 words; 3 = a short paragraph; 5 = several paragraphs or a few hundred words; 8 = a long multi-section post; 10 = an unusually extensive essay-length post); the number of separate worked examples, displays and enumerated steps; how much routine algebra or arithmetic is written out in full rather than compressed; and how often the same point, plan or conclusion is restated in different words ('so, to summarise', 'in other words', 'again, the idea is'). Count what is on the page; do NOT judge whether the detail is good, correct, useful, necessary, or well organised, and do NOT reward or penalise the quality of the exposition.
selected.rationale: This is the pure carrier of the parent, the countable bulk that the existing lint feature already tracks; isolating it here is what leaves D06 free to test whether any craft remains once bulk is removed. Two-way dissociation against D06 is given in D06's rationale: a three-line answer that closes the only real gap is 10/0 (D06/D07), while a thousand-word post that pads the easy steps and asserts the hard one is 0/10.

selected.name: Names a specific pitfall and explains why it fails
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the answer locates a specific mathematical failure mode -- an error, a misapplied theorem, a hidden assumption, a boundary or convergence trap -- and explains precisely why it fails, rather than only presenting a correct route. 10 = the failure is named and its mechanism shown, however tersely: 'The step that breaks is exchanging limit and integral: no dominating function exists here, as f_n = n on [0, 1/n] shows.' 5 = a real pitfall is named but its mechanism is only gestured at. 0 = no failure mode is identified at all, or only a vague gesture ('that is not quite right', 'be careful with the algebra', 'you need to be more rigorous') with nothing said about what goes wrong or why. Because the question body is NOT shown to you, judge only what the answer itself states about the pitfall -- do NOT try to verify it against anyone's actual work, and do NOT penalise the answer for pitfalls it might have missed. Do NOT reward warmth, encouragement, praise, second-person address, politeness, or sign-offs: a blunt, wholly impersonal answer must be able to score 10, and an effusively friendly one 0.
selected.rationale: The parent measures interpersonal wording, which mixes an affective habit with a real diagnostic skill -- knowing where reasoning about this kind of problem actually goes wrong and being able to say why. This component keeps only the diagnosis and explicitly bars the judge from crediting tone. Two-way dissociation against D09: (a) high here, low there -- 'The error is treating the sup as attained; on an open interval it need not be, so the extremal argument collapses' contains no second-person address at all, scoring 10 here and 0 on D09; (b) low here, high there -- 'Great question! You are doing fine, just be careful with your algebra and try again, hope this helps!' is saturated with coaching (D09 near 10) yet names no failure mechanism, scoring 0 here.

selected.name: Extent of second-person address, reassurance and imperative coaching
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of directly interpersonal wording aimed at the reader. Count and estimate coverage of: occurrences of 'you' and 'your'; imperatives directed at the reader ('note that', 'try', 'observe', 'convince yourself', 'go back and check'); reassurance, praise or encouragement ('good start', 'nice question', 'do not worry', 'you are almost there'); apologies and softening politeness; exclamation marks; and sign-offs ('hope this helps', 'good luck', 'let me know if anything is unclear'). 10 = second-person coaching pervades nearly every sentence from opening to sign-off. 5 = a handful of second-person turns in an otherwise impersonal post. 0 = wholly impersonal, with no 'you' and no address to the reader anywhere. Count the wording ONLY; do NOT decide whether the address is tactful, warranted, correct, or helpful.
selected.rationale: This is the mechanical, countable habit the parent is largely picking up, and the one the existing lint feature already tracks. It is kept deliberately narrower than D11: it counts affective and imperative address that attributes nothing, whereas D11 counts reproduction of the asker's own material. Two-way dissociation against D08 is stated in D08's rationale: an impersonal answer naming the exact interchange-of-limits failure is 10/0 (D08/D09), while a warm, encouraging post that locates nothing is 0/10.

selected.name: Lands the exact object asked, fully specialised to it
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the answer carries its argument to the specific object named in the question title, with this problem's own constants, exponents, index ranges, hypotheses and named objects substituted in, rather than stopping at a general theorem or a generic template the reader would still have to specialise. Use the title as the statement of the target as far as the title determines it; if the title fixes a specific quantity, condition or claim, require that the answer reach and state it. 10 = the asked object is reached and stated in the problem's own terms -- a closed form, the exact constant, the precise condition, the specific counterexample -- even in two plainly typed lines. 5 = the general machinery is set up and partly specialised but the final specific object is left to the reader. 0 = a general result is quoted or a standard method recited and the answer never lands on this particular case, however long, however well typeset, and however many worked examples of other cases it contains. Do NOT reward quoting the asker's words, second-person address, or any formatting; judge only specialisation to this problem.
selected.rationale: The parent's craft residue is tailoring: doing the last mile of work for THIS problem instead of handing over a template. Stated as reaching the titled object, it is judgeable from answer text plus title alone, and it is distinct from D08's craft (diagnosing a failure mode) because an answer can specialise perfectly while diagnosing nothing. Two-way dissociation against D11: (a) high here, low there -- 'For n = 7 the sum is 363/140, since the harmonic partial sums telescope against the given bound' quotes nothing, attributes nothing and contains no 'your', scoring 10 here and 0 on D11; (b) low here, high there -- an answer that block-quotes the asker's three lines, says 'your method' twice and 'as you did' once, then recites the general form of the ratio test without ever applying it to the series in the title scores near 10 on D11 and 0 here.

selected.name: Extent of verbatim echo and attribution of asker's material
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer reproduces, paraphrases, or explicitly attributes material to the asker. Count: block quotes of the question; quoted expressions, equations or lines of working attributed to the asker; attributive phrases such as 'your equation', 'your method', 'your integral', 'as you did', 'you wrote', 'you computed', 'you seem to be confused about', 'in your notation'; step-by-step restatement of the asker's own working before commenting on it; and addressing the asker by name or username. 10 = large parts of the post consist of quoted or restated asker material with explicit 'your ...' attributions running throughout. 5 = one quoted line or a couple of attributive phrases. 0 = nothing of the asker's is reproduced and nothing is attributed to them anywhere. Count the extent ONLY; do NOT judge whether the quoting is helpful, fair, or accurate. Do NOT count generic second-person coaching that attributes nothing to the asker ('note that', 'try', 'hope this helps') -- that belongs to a different criterion.
selected.rationale: This is the countable carrier of the parent: echoing the asker's text is a mechanical habit visible without any mathematical reading, and it is separated here from D09 by requiring attribution or reproduction rather than mere second-person tone. Two-way dissociation against D10 is stated in D10's rationale: a two-line answer that lands the exact titled value while quoting nothing is 10/0 (D10/D11), and a post that quotes the asker at length but only recites a general test is 0/10.

selected.name: LLM-Style Templated Boilerplate
selected.instruction: Score the extent to which the text uses generic, formulaic transitions typical of AI language models (e.g., 'To solve this problem, we can use...'). Do not judge the correctness or quality of the text.
selected.rationale: The dense model may flag over-explained, low-density LLM-style text as lower quality compared to human answers (R04 and R14 exhibit this heavily).
